title: Longest Cycle in a Directed Graph

monster.name: Vicious Ouroboros
monster.title: Emperor of Endless Recursions
monster.defeatQuote: Longest simple cycle in directed functional graph identified!

description: You are given a directed graph of `n` nodes labeled from 0 to `n - 1`, where each node has at most one outgoing edge. The graph is represented with an integer array `edges` where `edges[i]` denotes directed edge from node `i` to `edges[i]`. If node `i` has no outgoing edge, `edges[i] = -1`. Return the length of the longest cycle in the graph. If no cycle exists, return -1.
solutionCode:
def longestCycle(edges: list[int]) -> int:
    n = len(edges)
    visited = [False] * n
    ans = -1
    for i in range(n):
        if visited[i]: continue
        path = {}
        curr = i
        step = 0
        while curr != -1 and not visited[curr]:
            visited[curr] = True
            path[curr] = step
            step += 1
            curr = edges[curr]
        if curr != -1 and curr in path:
            ans = max(ans, step - path[curr])
    return ans
